header.title: PGM LI: Applied judicial curse: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Papyri Graecae Magicae
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:magic:dclp:64081:grc, from papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (CC BY 3.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY 4.0: credit papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (the source's own licence is CC BY 3.0) and this AI translation.

notes.1: Square brackets follow the edition’s restorations as nearly as English allows; words broken across lines are given whole on the line where they begin. Line 16 is damaged: the name of Hermes’ mother is lost and Eu...s is incomplete. Tereus is named as mother of both Neilammon and Harpocrates, whom Neilammon calls impious toward ‘me, the father’.

nodes.text: I entreat you, *nekydaimōn* [spirit of the dead],
and that which has befallen you,
[who] may [be wi]th me; not to hear
[as I am toward the g]ods; and them
